free.title: Charlie Parker Jazz Festival
free.caption:
New York throws Charlie Parker a birthday party in the two neighbourhoods he lived in - and it costs nothing.

The 34th Charlie Parker Jazz Festival takes over Marcus Garvey Park in Harlem on Friday and Saturday, then Tompkins Square Park in the East Village on Sunday. Saturday Aug 29 is Bird's actual birthday - he was born that day in 1920. Sunday's stage sits across from 151 Avenue B, his landmarked home, on a block the city co-named Charlie Parker Place.

Folding chairs are allowed at both parks, unlike Central Park SummerStage. Blankets and outside food are fine. No coolers, glass, cans, alcohol or bags over 16x16x8. Rain or shine, and there is no reschedule.

Full schedule: https://cityparksfoundation.org/charlieparker/

food.title: JAPAN Fes - East Village
food.caption:
Two East Village streets, two days, 34 Japanese food stalls - and no ticket.

JAPAN Fes runs a back-to-back double header in the East Village next weekend. Saturday takes Broadway between E 8th and E 9th with 18 stalls; Sunday moves one block to 4th Avenue between E 9th and E 10th with 16. Same hours both days, and the organisers have a $5 mini-bite menu running across vendors this season.

Get there at 10 - ramen and karaage lines are longest by early afternoon and popular items sell out. Bring cash and a card, the vendor mix is split. There is no seating.

Full lineup: https://www.japanfes.com/2026

art.title: The Black Mirror Experience
art.caption:
The only Black Mirror episode you can walk into - and it leaves New York on Sept 6.

The US premiere of The Black Mirror Experience is at The Shed in Hudson Yards. You put on an untethered VR headset and physically walk through the sets of a fictional tech company for about 60 minutes, in a group of 1 to 6, as the protagonist of an original standalone story. They scan your face and voice into an AI avatar called a LifeAgent on the way in (deleted after four weeks). It picked up a Special Mention in the Immersive Competition at Cannes 2026.

Save this one for a weekday evening, then walk the High Line south to Chelsea Market.

Tickets and full details: https://nyc.theblackmirrorexperience.com
